description.p: BedrockOnLinux installs and runs the Windows (GDK) edition of Minecraft Bedrock on Linux. One app does everything automatically:

ul.li: downloads the Minecraft version you pick;
provides native Friends, invitations, public Servers and Realms without scanning or rewriting the Minecraft process;
implements the WinAppSDK file picker used for world and skin imports;
verifies the engine, fixes curl/SSL, then launches the game.

description.p: Sign in, open Play • Servers, and join native Bedrock servers (Hive, CubeCraft, …) or crossplay/Geyser servers. No game files are shipped; you supply your own — you must own Minecraft.

screenshot.caption: The launcher: pick a version, sign in, play

description.p: Your Xbox friends can see you again while you play, the Microsoft sign-in no longer hangs on "Please wait" or dies part-way through, and the launcher stops downloading a version you never asked for.

ul.li: publishes the play session on Xbox Live, so the social tab stops saying you are offline and friends can invite you
keeps the sign-in window alive where the desktop runs accessibility, and opens the second leg of the sign-in the way Windows does, instead of on a page that never finishes
remembers which build you play, rather than reinstalling the newest one behind your back
lists every Minecraft build you have downloaded, what it weighs and removes the ones you are done with, in Settings ▸ Versions
fixes a download that failed on the downloader's own package cache, and leaves a log behind when one does fail
warns at PLAY when nothing is signed in for online play, instead of leaving Realms and servers quietly missing

description.p: Fixes the Play screen telling you to sign in to an account that is already linked, and a Minecraft download that ended on the licence Microsoft issued for it.

ul.li: keeps the Servers and Realms tabs reachable, and takes away the in-game sign-in button that could only ever fail — the account is linked from the launcher
says so when a Minecraft update moves the interface past those patches, instead of passing over them in silence
finishes a download whose licence Microsoft granted as a trial rather than outright
stops a download failing on a race against its own package cache, and counting past a hundred percent while it ran

description.p: Fixes a first install that could not fetch the game engine, adds controller navigation of the launcher window back, and shows the play session on Discord.

ul.li: fetches the game engine again on a first install, which 2.2.0 to 2.2.2 refused after its archive was rebuilt at the same address
drives the launcher window with a controller again, rewritten for the Qt window
shows what you are playing on Discord, and can be turned off
takes the version you highlighted in the picker, not the first one in the list

description.p: The launcher window is rebuilt on Qt, both Microsoft sign-ins now share one menu, and Minecraft shows up in Steam Deck Game Mode again.

ul.li: puts the sign-in that plays online and the one that downloads the game in a single menu, top right, and says why there are two
offers the download sign-in when PLAY needs it, instead of reporting a launch failure with nothing to act on
shows Minecraft in Steam Deck Game Mode, where the window was rendering but never presented
keeps the Microsoft Store sign-in across restarts, which also stops it filling the account's ten-device limit
switches between Stable and Preview without restarting first
ships a server you can join in the Servers tab
rebuilds the window on Qt: sharper text, correct DPI scaling and native Wayland output. Controller navigation of the launcher is gone for now and returns in a later release

description.p: The launcher can be driven with a controller, the Microsoft sign-in window opens on Wayland again, and a Store-downloaded Minecraft starts inside the Flatpak.

ul.li: navigates the whole window with a controller: the d-pad or left stick moves, A activates, B goes back, Start plays, so a Steam Deck no longer needs a mouse to reach PLAY
opens the Microsoft sign-in window on Wayland desktops where it used to die instantly, taking the game download with it
starts a Store-downloaded Minecraft from inside the Flatpak sandbox, and installs and starts it again on SteamOS
can close the launcher when the game starts, from Settings
finishes a first run that used to fail with "wineboot timed out" while the runtime it needs was still downloading
retries a Minecraft download that failed, instead of leaving a cache no later attempt could get past
reports in doctor what ray tracing the graphics stack granted the game on its last launch
says plainly that the achievements list loads but new achievements do not unlock yet

description.p: Minecraft is now downloaded from the Microsoft Store with your own account, and the launcher opens again in every session.

ul.li: downloads the game from the Microsoft Store with the account you link, using the licence that account holds, instead of a repackaged copy from a third-party repository: you must own Minecraft on that account to install it, and the Store sign-in is a second, separate link from the in-game one
keeps the choice of build, and adds the edition: Minecraft or Minecraft Preview, then any build, each in its own folder

plays a Store package whose executable stays encrypted on disk, by decrypting it into memory at launch; such a package needs the network and a valid Store session at every start, even for single-player
installs the game inside the Flatpak sandbox again: the manifest moved to the GNOME runtime, the only one carrying the WebKitGTK the Store sign-in window needs
stops the crash that hit the main menu as soon as an account was signed in
opens the launcher window in every session, including Steam Deck Game Mode, where the game had become unreachable; launching without the launcher stays available where it is asked for
names why the game is slow before it starts, and adds a ray tracing switch to Settings

description.p: Fixes the game freezing when its window is hidden, and makes the launcher reach the game from Steam Deck Game Mode.

ul.li: keeps the game running when its window is minimized or left on another virtual desktop: it used to come back black and never repaint, and turning on the legacy renderer was the only way out
starts the game directly when the launcher is opened in Steam Deck Game Mode, which shows one window at a time, so a single Steam entry reaches Minecraft
stops the packaged launcher from refusing to start in Game Mode, where it mistook Gamescope's display for a software renderer

description.p: Restores multi-threaded performance, lets the game start without the launcher window, and plays offline when Xbox Live is unavailable.

ul.li: builds the engine with Wine's in-process synchronization (ntsync) backend, which had been compiled out: every wait became a wineserver round-trip, so chunk generation stalled, the GPU idled and server tick rates collapsed
adds a direct launch shortcut, so Minecraft starts from the desktop, from Steam and from Steam Deck Game Mode without the launcher window in between
starts single-player and LAN play when no Microsoft account is linked or Xbox Live cannot be reached, instead of refusing to launch at all
ships an .rpm for the Fedora-based distributions and publishes nightly builds again

description.p: Restores Friends worlds over the internet and fixes Microsoft sign-out, the version picker and content importing.

ul.li: stops forcing a GnuTLS priority file that made Wine negotiate an unsupported TLS 1.3, which broke every in-game connection and left Friends worlds reporting world is full or publishing as LAN-only;
names an unsynchronized system clock when Xbox Live rejects the account, instead of blaming the Xbox profile;
removes the durable Microsoft refresh token from the Wine prefix on sign-out, and repairs the sign-out button itself;
scrolls the version picker with the wheel and places it correctly at 150% and 200% UI scaling;
rejects archive members escaping the destination directory when importing add-ons, worlds and templates;
recovers an interrupted first-run data migration and a wineboot that cannot resolve the RNG forward.

description.p: Fixes custom-skin selection, the in-game Achievements catalog and Flatpak startup with safe data migration.

ul.li: completes the single-file picker on Minecraft's calling apartment, avoiding a failing cross-apartment callback;
keeps the native picker attached to the game window in fullscreen and Gamescope sessions;
keeps graphics caches across game updates and prevents Advanced diagnostics from tracing hot GDK polling channels;
ships the fixes in the reproducible, attested wow64-archs-native12 managed engine.

description.p: Improves startup reliability across Linux desktops, LAN diagnostics and controller integration, and adds safer multi-profile and client workflows.

ul.li: handles X11, XWayland, Hyprland, Steam Game Mode, Steam Deck and multi-monitor dialogs automatically, including scaled and scrollable themed dialogs, global native-Wayland overrides and XWayland presentation recovery;
fixes Minecraft's in-game world and custom-skin picker with a pinned native WineGDK implementation;
migrates application data safely to the active XDG layout and keeps native, AppImage, Debian and Flatpak storage consistent;
configures SDL or Steam Input automatically for DualSense and DualSense Edge controllers;
adds isolated local Xbox profiles with shared large downloads protected by setup and launch locks;
repairs partial Wine prefixes and fixes Wine boot failures with a native cryptbase random-number implementation;
hardens external client DLL injection and reports immediate game crashes instead of claiming a false success;
strengthens downloads, archive imports, engine provenance, network diagnostics and release packaging.

description.p: Adds native Xbox services, working Friends and Realms, stable world and skin imports, and removes the Minecraft process-memory patcher.

ul.li: implements native XGame, XUser, token signing, gamertags, privileges and XSAPI context in WineGDK;
restores Friends, invitations, joining friends, public Servers and the dedicated Bedrock Realms authentication audience;
upgrades existing managed installations automatically and keeps engine replacement transactional and SHA-256 verified;
ships reproducible WineGDK source provenance and rejects any remnant of the former Minecraft memory-patch implementation.

description.p: Fixes the menu, ESC/back, pause, and dialog freeze reported in issues #27, #29, and #30 across both old and new Vulkan drivers.

ul.li: enables raw-VA root CBVs for Minecraft's indirect menu commands, preventing the render-thread stall while audio continues;
removes the launcher's redundant Vulkan hardware probe and lets the universal engine choose EXT/NV inside the game process;

reactivates the guarded Microsoft/Xbox server patches when an old compatibility preference survived an engine upgrade, while keeping an explicit per-revision troubleshooting fallback; and refuses incomplete or expired multiplayer token payloads, also on Python 3.9 and across Microsoft account changes;
adds a precise diagnostic when an old engine cannot create Minecraft's ExecuteIndirect command signatures.

description.p: Makes sure the graphics-engine fix from 1.2.8 actually reaches you: updating the launcher and pressing Play now updates the game engine automatically when a newer one has shipped. Before, the engine only updated if you re-ran Install/Update by hand, so the fix for the ESC/menu freeze silently missed people who just pressed Play — if it still froze for you on 1.2.8, this pulls the fixed engine in on the next launch.
Fixes the game freezing when you press ESC / back, pause, or dismiss an in-game dialog — mostly on newer graphics cards and drivers.

ul.li: updates the bundled graphics engine (DXVK and vkd3d-proton) to 3.0.1; the older version couldn't build one of Minecraft's draw commands and fell back to a path that hangs on recent GPUs, which is what caused the freeze on ESC / back / pausing / closing a popup;
after updating, launch once to download the new engine.

description.p: Fixes the game breaking when Advanced Diagnostics is on, and adds a clearer warning when your GPU isn't being used:

ul.li: if the game falls back to software rendering (your GPU's Vulkan driver isn't active), the launcher now tells you — that is what makes the Play screen render black; a reboot or driver reinstall fixes it.

description.p: Fixes online sign-in and two crashes:

ul.li: adds an optional setting to keep the mouse cursor inside the window, so it no longer slips outside the game in windowed mode.

description.p: Fixes a false "reinstall the game engine" warning that could appear after closing the game even when everything had worked: the post-game check was matching an unrelated, harmless system message. It now trusts the engine's own sign-in markers, so it no longer cries wolf on a perfectly good session.
A refreshed, modern interface and a fix for launch crashes on some systems:

ul.li: a new setting to turn off the in-game Servers-tab unlock: on a few systems forcing it makes the game freeze or crash a few seconds after launch, and turning it off lets the game run (Steam Deck, CachyOS and some others);
the version list and downloads are more reliable, and downloads now resume instead of failing on a flaky connection.

description.p: Fixes the AppImage hanging at "Preparing" with an empty version list on some Linux distributions. It now bundles its own certificate store, so it can always reach the download servers over HTTPS no matter where the system keeps its certificates — the version list, the game engine download and Microsoft sign-in all work out of the box. Completes the self-contained AppImage from 1.1.5.

The AppImage is now fully self-contained: it bundles its own Python and the Tk GUI toolkit, so it runs on any Linux out of the box with nothing to install first. This fixes the "tkinter is not installed" error on systems that ship Python without the Tk module. The Flatpak was already self-contained and the Debian package pulls those pieces in automatically; the portable .pyz still uses the system Python.

Fixes the launch crash on recent Minecraft builds (1.26.30+) the proper way, so the in-game Servers tab is unlocked everywhere instead of being greyed out on those builds. The "is signed in with Microsoft" patch now guards against the account object the game has not finished setting up yet: it keeps the flag where the object exists and safely does nothing where it is missing, so the game starts on every system (Steam Deck, CachyOS and others) and still shows the server list. Delivered by the engine auto-update.

Fixes a crash a few seconds after launch on recent Minecraft builds (1.26.30+): a binary patch was forcing an "is signed in with Microsoft" flag that those builds trust to access an account object that does not exist under Wine, causing a null dereference. The patch is now only applied on builds where it is safe; newer builds run normally (with a greyed Servers tab) instead of crashing. The fixed engine is delivered by the engine auto-update.

The bundled game engine now auto-updates: when a newer WineGDK engine is published, the launcher re-downloads it on the next launch — the same way the launcher updates itself — so the in-game sign-in and server-join fixes reach everyone, not just fresh installs.
Fixes after 1.1.0:

ul.li: the version picker now defaults to the version you last played (or the latest) instead of resetting to a different one;
the in-game sign-in and native-server-join binary patches now track the game across the 1.26.x updates.

description.p: Internal refactor into a Python package, with fixes for the open bug reports:

ul.li: fixes a startup crash and a spurious Steam launch caused by Proton's VR client;
fixes the Flatpak failing to start under a pure Wayland session;
makes Microsoft sign-in reliable by ensuring the required Python dependency is present on every install.

description.p: Flatpak packaging, plus two Wayland input fixes:

ul.li: opt-in gamescope (BOL_GAMESCOPE=1) so the in-game mouse works on Wayland sessions, where XWayland otherwise drops it;
the opt-in winewayland backend now falls back to XWayland automatically when it cannot open a window, so the game always starts.

description.p: Fixes for the opt-in winewayland backend and safer prefix repair.
